subject: Monthly remedy thresholds & burst-tolerance pilot — SLA template redline
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluebay.io>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueBay Procurement <procurement@bluebay.io>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA template questions — burst tolerance & monthly banding

Hi Stephanie / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BlueBay’s analytics team is enthusiastic about the performance we saw on peak inference bursts. Procurement has reviewed the standard SLA and we have two asks before we can move to redlines:

1) Burst tolerance pilot: During our end-of-quarter runs we expect short, intense spikes for 6–12 hours. We need an exception path that allows higher sustained tail latency for those windows without triggering full remedy payments, ideally for an initial 6-month pilot.

2) Monthly remedy smoothing: Instead of per-incident crediting, our finance team prefers a monthly smoothing approach (aggregate monthly remedy buckets). That helps forecasting for both sides.

Can Redwood propose a template amendment that accommodates a pilot for burst tolerance and a monthly smoothing mechanism with a clear cap? We’ve attached a short matrix from BlueBay that illustrates typical burst patterns.

Appreciate a short counterproposal by EOD tomorrow — procurement wants to include this in the upcoming SOW.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement, BlueBay Analytics
Alicia.Gomez@bluebay.io

Attachments: bluebay-remedy-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluebay.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA template questions — burst tolerance & monthly banding

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix, looks helpful.

High-level proposal we can stand behind:

- Burst tolerance pilot: 6-month pilot that elevates the tail-latency SLO for defined "scheduled burst windows" up to a 48-hour rolling window threshold. During pilot windows, incidents that fall within the declared schedule will not count toward the standard monthly remedy calculation as long as they remain below an absolute latency cap (we propose 2x baseline p95).

- Monthly remedy smoothing: Replace per-incident credits with an aggregated monthly remedy pool. Pool sizing: standard monthly pool equals 3% of monthly committed spend; for the pilot months we propose a temporary smoothing floor of 2% to limit variability. Any unspent portion of the pool rolls forward one month, up to a maximum carry-forward of 1.5% of monthly spend.

- Cap & guardrails: We propose a hard cap at 10% of monthly committed spend for any single month, with early termination rights for either party if an implementation materially degrades service for other customers.

I’ve attached a redline summary (PDF) that highlights where to update the template. Ben / Monica — can you review the proposed numbers and confirm legal/finance comfort? If this looks reasonable, I’ll send a tracked redline for BlueBay to mark up.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: 20261121-sla-redline-diff.pdf (summary, 4 pages)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluebay.io>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA template questions — burst tolerance & monthly banding

Alicia / Stephanie — quick commercial note from my side:

We like the pilot approach because it gives both teams telemetry to size the right remedy pool. A couple modifications from commercial:

- Pilot declaration window: BlueBay should designate burst windows up to 72 hours in advance for planned seasonality (we can accept emergency ad-hoc windows up to twice per quarter with a post-mortem).
- Temporary pilot discount: Redwood can offer a 10% uplift credit against monthly committed spend for the 6-month pilot period to offset BlueBay’s risk while we validate the smoothing model.
- Measurement: we'll use our token-level latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) tied to route ids you provide; these must be declared before pilot start.

If BlueBay accepts the commercial tweaks I’ll include them in the SOW numbers and ask finance to lock pilot accounting. Monica — please confirm any compliance or audit requirements around logging for the pilot.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluebay.io>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA template questions — burst tolerance & monthly banding

Thanks all — quick legal/ops confirmation:

- Logging & audit: Redwood will expose per-route logs and a monthly CSV export of incident tallies for the pilot. That meets BlueBay audit minimums; if you need raw KV-cache traces we can discuss a redaction process but that is out of scope for the pilot.
- Carry-forward / cap language: Monica suggests we qualify the carry-forward clause so it cannot be used to indefinitely defer remedy payment (i.e., maximum roll-forward window = 1 month and max carry cap = 1.5% of monthly spend).
- DocuSign: once Alicia confirms acceptance of the cap and pilot discount, I’ll circulate an SOW addendum to be signed (link included).

Alicia — would you like Redwood to run a 2-week instrumentation window prior to pilot start (no changes to credits, only data collection)? That will make the smoothing model much more accurate.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
